alternatives_rejected.why: Its latency deviation (E1) is smaller than ts-route-service's, and ts-route-service's own CPU and socket metrics also deviate (E3), so it is a downstream caller seeing the slowdown rather than the source.
Own-span self-time barely changed (1.23->1.58ms, E2) while the CPU metric rose 627.7% (E3). That fits CPU saturation better than an injected delay.
Socket deviation (z=19.53, 97.7%) is much weaker than CPU (z=62.57, 627.7%) in E3, so it is more likely a side effect.

proposed_fix.description: Verify CPU saturation or throttling on ts-route-service, then gate-approve either a modest CPU limit increase or an added replica, with rollback ready.
steps: Check whether ts-route-service pods are CPU-throttled (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods vs. total periods) and compare current CPU usage to requests and limits.
Check for a recent deploy, config change, or load increase on ts-route-service that coincides with the CPU and latency deviation onset (E1, E3).
Check the pod's own behavior (hot endpoints, request rate, GC or thread activity) to see whether the CPU rise is load-driven or erratic, per R2's 'check if application is performing normally'.
If throttling or saturation is confirmed and the app looks otherwise healthy, with human approval scale ts-route-service out by one replica (reversible) to spread load.

If the app is behaving erratically (another alert in the namespace firing) and throttling is confirmed, with human approval raise the CPU limit on the ts-route-service container only (requests unchanged), as R2 suggests for mixed alerts.
Watch ts-route-service latency-50/90 and CPU for 10-15 minutes after the change to confirm recovery; also check ts-admin-travel-service latency (E1), which is likely downstream of the route service.
preconditions: Confirm CPU saturation or throttling on ts-route-service pods is actually present, not just elevated usage.
Confirm the cluster or node has spare CPU capacity for another replica or a higher limit.
Confirm a human on-call has approved each change before it runs.
Record the current replica count and CPU requests/limits for rollback.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale ts-route-service back to the recorded replica count and restore the original CPU limit (e.g., revert the deployment spec via kubectl rollout undo or reapply the saved manifest).
